intro.data: A do-nothing step before a machine should change nothing. Two A→A steps are offered: one truly passes the value through, the other quietly smudges it (and then the Parser jams). Insert the real do-nothing step, then the Parser.
intro.alchemy: A do-nothing step before an apparatus should change nothing. Two A→A steps are offered: one truly preserves the material, the other taints it (and the Smelter jams). Insert the real do-nothing step, then the Smelter.
intro.spellcraft: A do-nothing step before a rune should change nothing. Two A→A steps are offered: one truly echoes the essence, the other warps it (and Ignition jams). Insert the real do-nothing step, then Ignition.
intro.abstract: A do-nothing step before f should change nothing. Of the two A→A steps, only the true identity leaves the value so f can act. Insert it, then f.

goal.data: Pass the input through a do-nothing step and then the Parser to reach the clean table.
goal.alchemy: Preserve the input, then run the Smelter to reach the ingot.
goal.spellcraft: Echo the input, then run Ignition to reach the flame.
goal.abstract: id_A then f, reaching the goal value.

description.data: looks like id, but alters it
description.alchemy: looks like id, but alters it
description.spellcraft: looks like id, but alters it

afterSuccess.data: The real Pass Through left the value untouched, so the Parser saw exactly what it always sees. The Smudger looked identical in type but changed the value and jammed the Parser. f ∘ id_A = f only for the true identity.
afterSuccess.alchemy: Preserve left the material untouched, so the Smelter saw what it always sees. The Tainter changed it and jammed. f ∘ id_A = f only for the true identity.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: Echo left the essence untouched, so Ignition saw what it always sees. The Warper changed it and jammed. f ∘ id_A = f only for the true identity.
afterSuccess.abstract: The identity left the value unchanged, so f behaved as itself: f ∘ id_A = f. The look-alike altered it and broke the chain.

reveal.summary: The identity law: composing a process with the identity leaves it unchanged. f ∘ id_A = f — but only for the genuine identity, which leaves every value exactly as it found it.
reveal.moreFormal: id_A is the two-sided unit for composition. Being A → A is not enough; identity must act as the do-nothing map on values.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: f(id(x)) === f(x), where id = (x) => x — a mutating look-alike would break this.
